questions.question: Does structural capacity become binding when held fixed long enough?
questions.conclusion: One serial synthetic dense-structure threshold cell reached frontier saturation and additive blocked pressure at every 11/12/13 ceiling in quantum 1; natural trajectories still did not bind.

questions.question: At what time/work level does it become binding?
questions.conclusion: In the one synthetic smoke cell, first frontier saturation and pressure occurred at quantum 1; no repeat-stable wall-clock estimate is claimed.

questions.question: Does extra capacity help after binding?
questions.conclusion: No matched binding state was available.

questions.question: Is capacity payoff delayed beyond one 250 ms quantum?
questions.conclusion: The continuing 1/2/4/8/16 oracle is implemented, but its broad cells were not run.

questions.question: Does capacity help before saturation?
questions.conclusion: Prior natural capacity-only arms were available but unused; this does not generalize to unseen binding states.

questions.question: Does effort help earlier than capacity?
questions.conclusion: Prior natural captures sometimes favored effort early while capacity was unused.

questions.question: At what effort level do returns diminish?
questions.conclusion: Anecdotal late saturation exists in the preceding natural report; no effort curve was run here.

questions.question: Does higher effort expose structural demand?
questions.conclusion: No controlled fixed-capacity effort ladder was executed.

questions.question: Does legacy expand before structural demand?
questions.conclusion: In the preceding natural 1 s/10 s line, recorded legacy expansions preceded observed frontier saturation/pressure.

questions.question: How often are legacy expansions ever used?
questions.conclusion: No newly opened range was observed used in the preceding natural line; the sample is small.

questions.question: Does new structural space produce better incumbents?
questions.conclusion: No productive new-slot event was observed; broader fixed/synthetic cells remain unrun.

questions.question: Can the candidate generator exploit additional slots?
questions.conclusion: In the synthetic dense smoke cell, generated, admitted, and polished frontier counts reached each 11/12/13 ceiling; the 13 ceiling also delivered 12 filters.

questions.question: Are blocked-capacity counters predictive?
questions.conclusion: They co-occurred with frontier saturation in the single synthetic cell, but predictive value across real/repeated states remains untested.

questions.question: Is frontier utilization predictive?
questions.conclusion: Frontier telemetry is available, but no predictive comparison was run.

questions.question: Is incumbent utilization predictive?
questions.conclusion: Incumbent utilization is recorded separately; no predictive study was run.

questions.question: Is residual magnitude predictive?
questions.conclusion: Prior residual magnitude/extrema did not distinguish useful expansion.

questions.question: Does a consistent filter-count knee exist?
questions.conclusion: No capacity-demand curves were generated in this bounded run.

questions.question: Is the knee case-dependent?
questions.conclusion: No cross-case knee sample exists yet.

questions.question: Does the search ever need very high filter ceilings?
questions.conclusion: No high-ceiling stress cells were run; ceiling utilization is not a score.

questions.question: Does quality improve monotonically with more allowed capacity under controlled continuation?
questions.conclusion: The one fixed-capacity synthetic threshold trajectory improved from 11 to 12 but regressed at 13. This is a single noisy serial sample, not a general capacity conclusion.

questions.question: Does quality improve monotonically with additional work on a preserved trajectory?
questions.conclusion: Continuing checkpoints are implemented; no repeated trajectory evidence was collected.

questions.question: How much run-to-run wall-clock variance remains?
questions.conclusion: Prior independent wall-clock trajectories were materially noisy; no new repeat distribution was run.

questions.question: Which search phases consume most work?
questions.conclusion: Raw counters and phase timing infrastructure exist, but no campaign aggregate was produced.

questions.question: How does runtime scale with delivered complexity?
questions.conclusion: No phase/runtime scaling sample was run.

questions.question: Do richer metrics agree with structural violation?
questions.conclusion: Rich metrics are now recorded without comparator changes; alignment requires result cells.

questions.question: Do extra filters create opposing/canceling structures?
questions.conclusion: Complexity observations include nearby opposing pairs; no delivered campaign sample was analyzed.

questions.question: Do high-Q solutions become quantization-sensitive?
questions.conclusion: Actual V2 quantization stress is implemented; no representative timing outputs were collected.

questions.question: Does quantization materially alter delivered quality?
questions.conclusion: The harness computes float-vs-delivered deltas; no campaign distribution is available.

questions.question: Is preamp correct after quantization?
questions.conclusion: The helper recomputes preamp through the existing dense-grid implementation; no broad stress report was run.

questions.question: How sample-rate-sensitive are delivered presets?
questions.conclusion: 44.1/48/96 kHz replay is implemented; no representative preset study was run.

questions.question: Are high-frequency solutions especially sample-rate-sensitive?
questions.conclusion: Upper-frequency synthetic family exists; no sample-rate result set was collected.

questions.question: Do conclusions generalize from development cases to holdout FR cases?
questions.conclusion: Holdout fixtures exist, but no frozen-policy comparison was authorized or run.

questions.question: Can the optimizer recover synthetic known-complexity targets?
questions.conclusion: The dense 12-component smoke case reached low but nonzero final error (best RMSE 0.04995); exact recovery has not been demonstrated.

questions.question: Does synthetic ground truth demonstrate genuine structural-capacity binding?
questions.conclusion: The dense smoke case produced immediate frontier saturation and additive pressure below/at/above known complexity, unlike the natural line. More repeats are required to quantify capacity payoff.

questions.question: Are real and synthetic capacity-demand patterns qualitatively consistent?
questions.conclusion: The synthetic and real result sets were not collected under one campaign.

questions.question: Does existing reseed/diversification help after local saturation?
questions.conclusion: No matched saturated state was run through the existing reseed arm.

questions.question: Is a dynamic structural-capacity scheduler actually necessary?
questions.conclusion: Prior natural evidence did not justify added scheduling complexity; synthetic/fixed evidence is still required.

questions.question: Is a dynamic effort allocator actually necessary?
questions.conclusion: Effort can be measured independently, but no allocator rule was frozen or tested.

questions.question: Is one simple joint allocator rule supported?
questions.conclusion: No rule is supported at this gate; policy work is intentionally held.

questions.question: Or is the safest architecture still observable resources plus simple fixed scheduling?
questions.conclusion: Yes as the current recommendation, pending fixed-capacity/synthetic result evidence.
